heading: ### Triggers T1–T3 and the re-pin rule

findings.quote:
the harness itself moved four times in
  one day (`597e1419…` → `b56c6e57…` → `4dc69ef9…` → `e3f838d4…` → `cf41efaa…`) [round 52: `4dc69ef9…` and `e3f838d4…` were working-tree writes, not commits (`plans/round-8.plan.md:69-74`, 15:27:40 and 15:28:38); the day's committed chain is `d8abee52…` (created 13:01) → `597e1419…` (13:57) → `b56c6e57…` (15:17) → `cf41efaa…` (16:06) → `75ed934d…` (18:28, r10-2 — `RerunSweep.md:93`) — four moves]
findings.why: The count and the chain it annotates cannot both be the day's tally: the parenthetical lists four transitions over `597e1419…`→`cf41efaa…` but two of them (`4dc69ef9…`, `e3f838d4…`) are, by the same bracket, non-commits, while the bracket's own four-move committed chain runs `d8abee52…`→`75ed934d…` and shares neither endpoint — git shows seven distinct harness states on 2026-10-14 (d8abee52 13:01:03, 597e1419 13:57:18, b56c6e57 15:17:26, cf41efaa 16:06:31, 75ed934d 18:28:23 as commits; 4dc69ef9 and e3f838d4 as no-commit writes), so the sentence's list and its 'four times' disagree.
